title: Introduce batch-affinity optimizer and 'quant-sentinel' graceful quantization profile
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Adds batch-affinity optimizer to improve request packing for tenant/route locality and introduces a new quantization profile 'quant-sentinel' that allows graceful degradation across capacity tiers. Includes telemetry hooks and a unit-econ dry-run CLI to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs.
description: Motivation: We have recurring tenant noise and suboptimal packing when multiple small requests with similar token shapes hit the same serving pool. Current batching is agnostic to tenant affinity which causes more KV cache misses and inefficient GPU utilization. Additionally, aggressive quantization rollouts have caused occasional quality regressions for tail workloads. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) a batch-affinity optimizer that prefers packing requests with high locality (tenant, route, prompt-shape signatures) while respecting latency SLOs and (2) a conservative 'quant-sentinel' quantization profile that progressively reduces precision by lane and includes a rollback sentinel that forces fallback to a safe quantized variant on quality regressions. Design/changes summary: - Routing/packing: new affinity scoring module (affinity_score) that computes a lightweight locality score using tenant_id, model_version, prefix hash, and token-length bucket. The packer will bias towards high-affinity groups while still respecting pack size and latency headroom. - Prefill/cache: added an affinity-aware prefill hint that enables soft KV cache pinning for high-affinity lanes (TTL-based, configurable per-tenant). - Quantization: added a new profile 'quant-sentinel' that annotates model variants with a sentinel threshold and a staged degradation path: fp16 -> int8-symmetric -> int8-symmetric+kv-compress. Each stage has quality gates and automatic fallback to a verified baseline when regressions are detected. - Telemetry/metrics: new metrics (batch_affinity_ratio, affinity_pack_efficiency, quant_sentinel_fallbacks) and tracing tags (affinity_group_id, quant_stage) for post-deploy analysis. - CLI/tooling: unit-econ dry-run flag to 'redwood-econ' CLI to simulate per-tenant cost delta with current traffic shape and proposed affinities/quant profiles. Rollout plan: 1) Canary deploy optimizer into one region with 5% traffic for non-enterprise tenants for 48 hours. 2) Collect metrics and run quality probes (eval set + live A/B) using the quant sentinel gate. 3) Ramp to 50% with telemetry gates, then to 100% if no regressions. Checklist: - [x] affinity scoring unit tests - [x] packer integration tests with latency SLOs - [x] quant-sentinel unit tests and sentinel regression hooks - [x] telemetry dashboards (draft) - [x] CLI dry-run implemented - [x] e2e smoke test in benchmark-lab Observability notes: initial smoke benchmarks show a 9-12% token/sec utilization increase for mixed small-request workloads and a 7-9% median latency decrease for 0-128 token requests under load. Quality gate simulated on our eval set shows <0.5% delta for the first quant stage, and 1.5-2.1% for stage 2 for large-context prompts (above 1024 tokens) — hence the sentinel fallback behavior. Motivation references: ENG-1892 (tenant packing problems), ENG-2041 (quant rollout safe paths), SUP-4123 (customer incident showing regression during quant rollout).

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Nice end-to-end. Two questions: 1) affinity_score weight defaults — do we expose them per-tenant or keep globally tuned? 2) any extra memory / KV pin risk under heavy churn?
Ava Chen: Reply: default weights are global tuned but exposed via tenant override flags; KV pin uses TTL and eviction heuristics to prevent unbounded memory growth (added tests).
Priya Nair: Please add canary gating based on affinity_pack_efficiency and quant_sentinel_fallbacks; ensure rollback hook can be invoked from console.
Ava Chen: Reply: added telemetry gates and console runbook; rollback is a one-click toggle that flips traffic to baseline variant (documented in docs/deployment/quant-sentinel.md).
Samir Patel: Lgtm after minor nits — prefer explicit timeouts in packer loop and a small comment about potential fairness regressions for small tenants. Added a requested change on packer.go
Ava Chen: Addressed nits, added timeout and fairness limiter; ran bench again and attached numbers.
